passage: The novelist Chinua Achebe wrote Things Fall Apart (1958) partly in response to European novels that portrayed African societies as without history or order. Achebe filled his novel with detailed descriptions of Igbo law, religion, farming, and storytelling. A reader familiar with the novels Achebe was responding to would most likely conclude that these descriptions ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: were meant to show that Igbo society had complex institutions those novels had ignored.
were included mainly because Achebe expected readers to know Igbo society well.
were copied from the European novels that Achebe had read as a student.
were intended to show that Igbo society had no history before Europeans arrived.
steps: Achebe was answering novels that showed African societies as lacking history or order.
Detailed law, religion and farming directly counter that portrayal.
The other choices contradict his purpose or have no support in the text.
key: Read the stated purpose; the details serve it.
